summary: Robert DeCaroli is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his MA and PhD from UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper, and held posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount University, and George Mason University.

Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1977 to 1981. He held academic posts at the University of Kerala and the Université catholique de Louvain around 1989.

Robert Duquenne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He worked at Hōbōgirin as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism (attested 1981) and was associated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, and Padmanabh S. Jaini, and with Kusan Sunim. He served as a professor at UCLA, attested from 1986 to 1994.

Robert E. Morrell was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic post at Washington University in St. Louis, attested in 1985 and 2006.

Robert E. Svoboda is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oklahoma and with mentor Vimalananda. In 2008, he was attested as an adjunct member at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested between 1993 and 2014, and held a post in the Otani Society.

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University, and was later an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria, attested between 2000 and 2005.
Robert Ford Campany is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He served as a professor at Indiana University from circa 1989 to 2010 and joined the faculty at Vanderbilt University around 2010.

Robert Gardner was a scholar of Indology who studied at Harvard University from circa 1944 to 1948. He held an academic post at the University of Puget Sound and served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1957 to 1997.

Robert H. Brower was a Japanology scholar who studied at Harvard University and the University of Michigan. He served as Chairman of the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at the University of Michigan from circa 1966 to 1988.

Robert H. Sharf is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. He taught at McMaster University, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1956 to 1989 and also held a professorship at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert Kritzer is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University, attested between 1999 and 2017.

Robert L. Brown was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 1986 to 2014 and a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

Robert Lenz was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Tartu Governorate Gymnasium and the Imperial University of Dorpat before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1835 to 1836.

Robert M. Gimello was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He served as department head and professor emeritus at the University of Arizona, and as a professor at Harvard University.

Robert Maclagan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and Addiscombe Military Seminary, later serving as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from Princeton University. He served as Distinguished Chair Professor at National Taiwan University and Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies at Assumption University.

Robert Mayer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University, supervised by Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and served on the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford in 2002.
